channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan to Cooperate on Drip Irrigation Systems
item.description: A Kyrgyz delegation visited Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan to discuss implementing drip and sprinkler irrigation. Memorandums of understanding were signed with companies in Almaty and Tashkent. These agreements aim to introduce water-saving technologies in Kyrgyzstan, improving water resource efficiency for agricultural lands.

item.title: Uzbekistan Declares Decade of National Rise, Prioritizing Education and Knowledge
item.description: Uzbekistan has declared the upcoming decade as an era of National Rise, emphasizing education and knowledge as key drivers of development. The first of seven national programs focuses on developing human capital by improving education from preschool to higher levels. The president stressed the crucial role of teachers in this national progress.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Ministry Unveils Plan to Stabilize Prices Through 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Ministry has presented a government plan for 2026-2027 to stabilize prices for goods and services. Measures include importing livestock and wheat, building warehouses, supporting farmers, and controlling fuel costs. The goal is to keep inflation between 7.7-8.5 percent in 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Launch Pilot 'Green AI' Module for Agricultural Recommendations
item.description: Uzbekistan will pilot a 'Green AI' module to analyze soil composition, climate, and water supply in different regions. The system will provide recommendations on suitable areas and tree species for planting, optimizing agricultural practices.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Combating Cybercrime and Raising Public Awareness
item.description: Uzbekistan is intensifying efforts against cybercrime, a key state policy priority. New measures aim to prevent and counter cyber threats, with a focus on educating citizens about cybersecurity. Scammers often use messaging apps, employing urgency and psychological pressure.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Transport Ministry Proposes Digital System to Combat Shadow Economy
item.description: The shadow economy in Uzbekistan's freight transport sector exceeds 42 percent. The Ministry of Transport has proposed creating a unified digital transport system to legalize informal services. This initiative aims to establish a registry of carriers and an electronic system for orders and services, enhancing transparency and convenience.

item.title: Transformations in Karakalpakstan Aim for Human Dignity and Honor
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's recent visit to Karakalpakstan assessed transformations initiated in 2017. State policy focuses on expanding citizens' opportunities through new enterprises, healthcare, and education. Economic development is linked to social problem-solving and future confidence, addressing issues like Aral Sea consequences, soil salinization, and migration pressures.

item.title: Tajikistan's Petroglyphs Included in UNESCO Preliminary List
item.description: Five petroglyph complexes in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan region and four historical-natural sites in Khatlon region are now on UNESCO's Preliminary World Heritage List. The Agency for Protection of Historical and Cultural Heritage stated these sites represent valuable historical and cultural heritage, crucial for studying ancient civilizations and regional development.

item.title: Uzbekistan explores participation in Nakhichevan railway construction project
item.description: Uzbekistan is exploring the possibility of participating in the construction of the Nakhichevan railway, a project that would provide access to Turkey's Samsun and Istanbul ports. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to make Uzbekistan a key link in the shortest land route from the Pacific to Europe, aiming to double transport services by 2030.

item.title: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway construction to expand, impacting regional trade
item.description: Construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is set to expand, a development expected to alter the region's map and reduce import costs. This infrastructure project holds significant importance for Tajikistan, potentially facilitating cheaper trade and improved connectivity.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans 17 New Logistics Centers and Terminals
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish 17 new logistics centers and terminals. These projects are slated for implementation in Tashkent city and the Tashkent, Andijan, Surxondaryo, and Buxoro regions, according to a meeting chaired by the President.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Invest $200 Million in Railway Modernization
item.description: Uzbekistan may allocate $200 million for railway modernization. The funds are intended to increase the capacity of the Maktaaral-Sirdaryo, Angren-Pop, Toshguzor-Boysun-Qumkurgan, Tashkent-Samarkand, and Toqimachi-Angren sections by 25-30%.

item.title: Tajikistan Presents "One Health" Approach at FAO Global Conference
item.description: Tajikistan shared its national experience in food security and sustainable production systems at the FAO Global Conference on "One Health" in agro-food systems in Rome. The conference, held September 21-23, focuses on practical applications of the "One Health" approach to enhance food security and resilience.

item.title: UN Warns of Mass Displacement Due to Sea Level Rise by Century's End
item.description: The United Nations warns that a potential half-meter rise in sea levels by the end of the century could force between 150 to 300 million people to leave their homes. Scientists have not ruled out this scenario, highlighting the significant threat of climate change-induced displacement.

item.title: Four Arrested in Tashkent Region for Operating Drug Laboratory in Rented Apartment
item.description: Four individuals were apprehended in Chirchiq, Tashkent region, for allegedly operating a drug laboratory in a rented apartment to produce and sell narcotics. The State Security Service reported the operation involved processing hashish oil and semi-finished products.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Implements New Registration Rules for Foreigners and Stateless Persons
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has updated its registration procedures for foreigners and stateless individuals. The new rules aim to streamline registration, clarify document and accommodation requirements, and establish uniform standards for various foreign national categories. Registration must occur after entry and by the last day of permitted stay without prior registration.

item.title: Uzbekistan Official Explains New Party Registration Process and Government Reforms
item.description: Tohirjon Safarov, deputy head of the Agency for Strategic Development and Reforms, clarified issues concerning the registration of new parties and initiative groups. He also addressed government downsizing and the opening timeline for the Public Chamber.

item.title: Earthquake in Tajikistan Felt in Uzbekistan's Fergana Valley with Intensity of 2 Points
item.description: An earthquake originating in Tajikistan on September 21 registered a magnitude of 4.9 with a depth of 160 km. The tremors were felt in Uzbekistan's Fergana region, including Sokh, Quvasoy, and Fergana districts, with an intensity of 2 points.

item.title: Almalyk Mining and Metallurgical Company receives Ba2 credit rating from Moody's
item.description: The Almalyk Mining and Metallurgical Company (AMMC) has obtained a credit rating of "Ba2" with a "Stable" outlook from Moody's. AMMC also received an independent credit assessment (BCA) of "ba3".

item.title: Dushanbe to host first Asian Parliamentary Assembly committee meeting
item.description: Dushanbe will host the first meeting of the Asian Parliamentary Assembly's Standing Committee on Social and Cultural Issues from September 24-27, 2026. Tajikistan holds the committee's chairmanship for 2026-2027.

item.title: Uzbek citizen who fought for Russia in Ukraine sentenced to 4 years
item.description: A 31-year-old Uzbek citizen, who fought for Russia in the Ukraine conflict, has been sentenced to four years in prison by a court in the Samarqand region. He reportedly joined the Russian military to avoid prosecution for drug offenses.

item.title: Kazakh prosecutor tells Chechen activist he could become a martyr
item.description: A Kazakh prosecutor reportedly told Chechen activist Movlayev, who twice attempted suicide after being denied refugee status, that he could become a martyr. The Cassation Court upheld previous decisions refusing his asylum claim.

item.title: Tajikistan presents report on child rights to UN Committee in Geneva
item.description: Tajikistan's delegation, led by the Justice Minister, presented its periodic national report to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child in Geneva. The report detailed the country's progress in implementing the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

item.title: Mayor of Guliston promises resumption of Adrasmon mining plant operations in September
item.description: The mayor of Guliston has pledged that the Adrasmon ore processing plant will resume operations in September. The reason for the plant's previous shutdown remains unclear, though it was established in the latter half of the 20th century.

item.title: Man suspected of embezzling 5 billion soums extradited from Turkey to Uzbekistan
item.description: A man, S.A., wanted internationally for allegedly embezzling 5 billion soums by misappropriating credit funds, has been apprehended in Turkey and returned to Uzbekistan. The Istanbul Consulate reported the extradition. He faces charges under Article 167 of the Criminal Code.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev's visit to Karakalpakstan spurs new development projects
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's visit to Karakalpakstan marks a significant step for the region's development. Projects worth $7.6 billion have been launched, focusing on economic diversification, industrial growth, and job creation. Regional GDP has surged from 8.5 trillion soums in 2016 to over 54 trillion soums.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Loan Portfolio Exceeds 644 Trillion Soums, Growing by 68 Trillion in One Year
item.description: The total loan debt of the population and businesses to banks in Uzbekistan has surpassed 644.63 trillion soums. This figure represents an increase of 68.4 trillion soums over the past year, indicating significant growth in lending.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Establish World-Class Cell Technology Center for Advanced Research and Treatment
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to build a world-class cell technology center to become a global hub for advanced cell-based research, production, and patient treatment. The initiative aims to elevate the country's capabilities in regenerative medicine.

item.title: Tajik Court Sentences Man to 22 Years for Stabbing Police Major
item.description: A 27-year-old man has been sentenced to 22 years in prison in Tajikistan's Sughd region for stabbing a police major. The incident occurred on May 12 near the Syr Darya river in Khujand. The officer, who intervened in a dispute, was stabbed multiple times but recovered and returned to duty.

item.title: Uzbekistan Banks Prevent Over 18 Million Fraudulent Transactions
item.description: Uzbekistan's banks prevented over 18 million fraudulent transactions in the first half of 2026. Antifraud and antivirus systems also cleaned malware from 2 million devices. Further details are available online.

item.title: Moscow Faces Mass Drone Attack on Election Day; Ballistic Missile Mentioned
item.description: Moscow experienced a mass drone attack on election day, with reports suggesting the use of a "Pelican" ballistic missile. Several facilities, including an oil refinery, sustained significant damage. Further details are available online.

item.title: Latvian President: Most NATO States Cannot Repel Russian Missile Attacks
item.description: The Latvian president stated that most NATO countries cannot repel Russian missile attacks. He highlighted significant challenges in European and NATO air defense. Russia may attempt to advance on the front lines during winter. Further details are available online.

item.title: Uzbekistan Places Businessman Mominjon Yuldashev on International Wanted List
item.description: Uzbekistan has placed businessman Mominjon Yuldashev, from the Fergana region, on the Interpol wanted list. He is sought for embezzlement under Article 167 of the Criminal Code. Yuldashev has previously been involved in business dealings in Belarus and had sanctions imposed by the World Bank.

item.title: Chinese investor discovers 4 tons of gold reserves in Uzbekistan's Karakalpakstan
item.description: A Chinese investor has identified 4 tons of gold reserves on 200 hectares of land in Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan, following a $33 million investment. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced plans to expand geological exploration and establish a gold mining and processing cluster creating 1,000 jobs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank removes "Zolotaya Korona" from electronic money systems registry
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has canceled the registration of the Russian payment system "Zolotaya Korona" based on the operator's request. The system, registered in Kyrgyzstan in 2016, also operates as an international money transfer operator. Eight registrations have been annulled this year.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Social Fund Reports Surplus but Faces Budget Dependence
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Social Fund reported a surplus of approximately 3 billion soms for 2025, with revenues around 130 billion and expenses 127 billion. However, 44.4 billion soms came from the state budget, indicating significant dependence. Pensioner purchasing power decreased due to rising prices.

item.title: Kyrgyz President visits Utah Olympic Park, studies winter sports development
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov visited Utah Olympic Park during his US trip. He met with the 2034 Winter Olympics organizing committee chair and learned about sports infrastructure development and legacy use. Japarov noted Utah's experience is valuable for Kyrgyzstan's winter sports potential.

item.title: Emomali Rahmon begins working trip to Sughd region
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon arrived in the Sughd region for a working trip on September 20. The visit aims to open new facilities, assess the socio-economic situation, meet residents, and participate in events marking the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's independence. The trip focuses on state development and economic progress.

item.title: Interpol identifies 126 terrorists using AI in Operation Shams II
item.description: Interpol has identified 126 foreign fighters through the use of artificial intelligence (AI) during anti-terrorism Operation Shams II. The operation, led by Interpol with specialists from 11 countries, analyzed over 108,000 images shared by jihadists. AI tools helped remove duplicates and enhance image quality, reducing the dataset for facial recognition.

item.title: Uzbekistan allocated 18.3 trillion soums in mortgage loans over 8 months
item.description: In Uzbekistan, 18.3 trillion soums were allocated for mortgage loans in the first eight months of the year. Approximately 74% of these loans were for the primary market. Data also revealed the age distribution of loan recipients and the proportion of men and women among them.
